stories.headline: PM Ruginienė's televised interview sparks social media backlash over competence and communication
stories.summary: An interview between political scientist Rima Urbonaitė and PM Inga Ruginienė on Laisvės TV triggered a wave of public criticism after Ruginienė struggled to answer pointed questions and visibly grew irritated; reaction from commentators, celebrities, and the LSDP itself dominated public discourse for several days. Urbonaitė later explained her approach, while critics including law professor Egidijus Kūris and singer Marijonas Mikutavičius publicly piled on.

stories.headline: 30,000 rally in Vilnius against LRT law amendments as parliamentary debate drags on
stories.summary: Around 30,000 demonstrators gathered in Vilnius Cathedral Square on Saturday to oppose proposed amendments to the law governing public broadcaster LRT, which critics say would allow political interference; PM Ruginienė changed her public tone to calls for 'peace' after an unannounced LSDP faction meeting, while Seimas speaker Juozas Olekas drew criticism for saying a tree-planting event was more meaningful than the protest.

stories.headline: Police open investigation after recording pen found at closed LSDP council meeting, LRT journalist accused
stories.summary: Police launched a pre-trial investigation after LSDP reported finding a pen with hidden audio-recording equipment at a closed party council session; the party accused LRT journalist Eglė Samoškaitė of planting it, while LRT administration denied any wrongdoing. The incident has become entangled with the broader LRT law controversy, with LSDP framing it as evidence of hostile journalism.

stories.headline: Former PM Paluckas faces illicit enrichment charges; suspends LSDP membership and waives immunity
stories.summary: The Prosecutor General requested removal of parliamentary immunity for former PM and current MP Gintautas Paluckas over suspected illicit enrichment; Paluckas confirmed he suspended his LSDP membership and would waive immunity via simplified procedure. LSDP leader Sinkevičius said Paluckas could continue working in the parliamentary faction, while President Nausėda and PM Ruginienė urged restraint pending the legal process.

stories.headline: Pension reform fallout: 40% of 2nd-pillar participants withdraw funds, spending boom documented
stories.summary: Data showing approximately 40% of second-pillar pension fund participants have withdrawn their accumulated savings since the reform took effect triggered wide political debate; PM Ruginienė defended the reform and noted rising consumption with satisfaction, while President Nausėda discussed possible future flexibility on mandatory annuities and the Bank of Lithuania weighed in on system attractiveness. Analysts estimated roughly half the ~3 billion euros withdrawn was flowing into retail spending.

stories.headline: Nausėda at Cyprus EU summit: pushes Ukraine accession, defense-industry cooperation, eastern flank budget focus
stories.summary: President Nausėda traveled to Cyprus for an informal European Council session, meeting Ukrainian President Zelensky, Cypriot President Christodoulides, and other EU leaders; he called for immediate launch of Ukraine's EU accession chapters, called for real defense-industry cooperation with Ukraine, warned that the EU's 2028–2034 budget lacks sufficient focus on the eastern flank, and opposed suspension of the EU-Israel association agreement.

stories.summary: The informal EU summit in Cyprus centered on clarifying the bloc's mutual defense clause (Article 42.7) amid US President Trump's criticism of NATO allies over the Iran war and a leaked Pentagon memo suggesting Spain could be suspended from NATO; EU leaders including Nausėda (covered separately in story 6) debated whether EU defense integration complements or risks undermining NATO, with Macron declaring the EU clause 'stronger' than NATO's Article 5.

stories.headline: Seimas approves new Kapčiamiestis military training ground and Tauragė range expansion despite local opposition
stories.summary: Lithuania's parliament voted to establish a new military training facility at Kapčiamiestis (near the strategically vital Suwałki corridor) and to expand the existing Tauragė range into Jurbarkas district, overcoming objections from local residents and some within the governing coalition; the decisions were framed as responses to the deteriorating regional security environment.

stories.headline: Divergent Lithuanian reactions to Zelensky's warnings about Russian threat to Baltic states
stories.summary: After Ukrainian President Zelensky publicly warned of a possible Russian threat to the Baltic states, Lithuanian officials offered contrasting responses: PM Ruginienė called for avoiding 'alarmist rhetoric,' while TS-LKD leader Landsbergis argued Zelensky likely had serious grounds and urged Lithuanians to prepare rather than get agitated; Estonian intelligence separately assessed no direct attack threat.

stories.headline: Lithuania's mandatory military draft expansion draws international attention
stories.summary: Multiple international and domestic outlets covered Lithuania's recently reformed conscription policy expanding draft eligibility to all 18-to-22-year-old men; reporting noted a pragmatic rather than purely patriotic motivation among young Lithuanians, with volunteer numbers up sharply since 2022 and special operations forces also conducting intake selection.

stories.headline: Ruginienė denies tasking foreign minister to arrange Trump meeting
stories.summary: PM Ruginienė denied a media report that she had instructed Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys to arrange a meeting with US President Trump; she also denied having raised the matter through back channels and said the relationship with the president functions as a 'tandem.' The denials prompted further questions about her international ambitions and relationship with Budrys.

stories.headline: NATO intercepts Russian bombers over Baltic; Russia threatens European hosts of French nuclear-capable jets
stories.summary: NATO fighters including French Rafales based at Šiauliai Air Base in Lithuania intercepted Russian strategic bombers and fighter jets flying over the Baltic Sea; separately, Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister warned that European countries hosting French nuclear-capable Rafales would be added to priority target lists, with Lithuanian and Latvian presidents publicly engaging with the nuclear burden-sharing proposal.

stories.headline: Lithuania's MoD moves to procure Merops anti-drone interceptors tested in Ukraine
stories.summary: Lithuania's Ministry of Defence announced it is considering purchasing a test batch of Merops AS-3 Surveyor drone-intercepting systems without a standard tender, citing urgency; the system has been combat-tested in Ukraine and is described as compatible with Lithuania's existing air defense architecture.

stories.headline: Nausėda calls for Rosatom sanctions on Chernobyl 40th anniversary
stories.summary: On the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster, President Nausėda called for international sanctions against Russian nuclear energy company Rosatom, linking Russia's nuclear threats against Ukrainian nuclear facilities to the Chernobyl legacy; his call was noted internationally alongside similar commemorative events.

stories.headline: Ruginienė calls for gender balance in diplomat appointments, criticizes Foreign Ministry
stories.summary: PM Ruginienė publicly urged the Foreign Ministry to apply gender balance principles when appointing diplomats, in remarks that were interpreted by some as another sign of friction between the PM and Foreign Minister Budrys.

stories.headline: PM's official motorcade criticized for high-speed urban driving; Ruginienė pledges to moderate
stories.summary: Conservative MP Mindaugas Lingė raised the issue of PM Ruginienė's escort convoy regularly speeding through Vilnius streets during a parliamentary Government Hour; Ruginienė acknowledged the criticism and promised to pay attention, in what became a minor public image episode.

stories.headline: Public trust poll shows Nausėda leading all figures; Ruginienė ranks tenth
stories.summary: A new Baltic Surveys poll commissioned by ELTA found President Nausėda as the most trusted public figure in Lithuania at 10.4%, down from 13% in December; PM Ruginienė ranked tenth at 3.4%, while media figure Andrius Tapinas and Dawn of Nemunas leader Remigijus Žemaitaitis placed in the top rankings.

stories.summary: Ignitis Group CFO Jonas Rimavičius stated that the company's exceptional green energy investment expansion phase is 'essentially over' and the investment profile will shift; separately, Ignitis subsidiary CEO Artūras Bortkevičius announced he intends to seek a second mandate when his current term ends.
